disclaimer: Figures here are background from public labeling and research descriptions. They are not medical advice, not a dose for you, and not a protocol. Approved medicines follow their own prescribing information. Many entries are unapproved, and human dosing is often not established. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently.

categories.title: Growth hormone / secretagogues
categories.summary: GHRH analogs, ghrelin-receptor agonists, and related compounds discussed for growth-hormone signaling.

categories.title: Metabolic / GLP agonists
categories.summary: Incretin and related hormone agonists studied for glucose and body-weight regulation.

categories.title: Healing & recovery
categories.summary: Peptides discussed mainly from preclinical wound, tissue, or connective-tissue research.

categories.title: Cognitive / nootropic
categories.summary: Peptides studied for attention, anxiety, or other central-nervous-system effects.

categories.title: Fat loss
categories.summary: Compounds whose published work emphasizes fat mass or lipolysis rather than a broad endocrine effect.

categories.title: Sexual health
categories.summary: Melanocortin, kisspeptin, and GnRH-related compounds discussed for sexual function or reproductive signaling.

categories.title: Immune / inflammation
categories.summary: Peptides studied for host defense or immune modulation.

categories.title: Sleep
categories.summary: Peptides discussed in sleep research. Evidence is often limited.

categories.title: Other
categories.summary: Entries that do not sit cleanly in one of the groups above.

peptides.name: Tesamorelin
peptides.summary: A synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone, stabilized against rapid breakdown.
peptides.mechanism: It acts on GHRH receptors in the pituitary and raises pulsatile growth hormone, with downstream effects on IGF-1. US approval is for reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-associated lipodystrophy, not for general fat loss or athletic use.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved as Egrifta and Egrifta SV for a specific HIV-related indication. Other uses are outside that labeling.
peptides.dosingNotes: US labeling has included a 2 mg once-daily injection (Egrifta) and a later 1.4 mg once-daily product (Egrifta SV). Those are labeled doses for the approved indication. Check the current prescribing information. Other amounts discussed outside that label vary; verify independently. This is not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: The approved products are lyophilized vials with a diluent volume specified in the prescribing information. Research vials sold outside that kit are a different presentation. Volumes discussed for those vials are not standardized and are not instructions.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Like other GHRH analogs it is short-acting, which is why the approved products are dosed once daily rather than weekly.
peptides.safetyNotes: Labeling discusses glucose effects, injection-site reactions, fluid retention, and hypersensitivity. People with an active malignancy history are called out in the prescribing information. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Ipamorelin
peptides.summary: A selective ghrelin-receptor agonist studied as a growth-hormone secretagogue.
peptides.mechanism: It stimulates growth-hormone release from the pituitary. In preclinical comparisons it produced less cortisol and prolactin rise than older ghrelin mimetics such as GHRP-2 and GHRP-6. It is not a GHRH analog.
peptides.researchStatus: Not an FDA-approved medicine. Human therapeutic dosing is not established by a labeling authority.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary and are often described in the hundreds of micrograms, once or more per day. Those figures are not a labeled dose. Verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials discussed in research-chemical listings are often 2 mg, 5 mg, or 10 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Commonly cited around 2 hours. Confirm in a primary source before relying on that figure. Discussions often pair it with a short-acting GHRH analog; pairing is a forum pattern, not evidence of a required schedule.
peptides.safetyNotes: Human safety data are limited. Hunger, water retention, and tingling are commonly mentioned anecdotes, not a characterized adverse-event profile. In October 2026, a coroner in Victoria, Australia, found that a man died of anaphylaxis after self-injecting compounded CJC-1295 with ipamorelin, at double his prescribed amount, and recommended that the TGA review these peptides. One case does not measure overall risk. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: CJC-1295 without DAC
peptides.summary: A short-acting modified growth hormone-releasing hormone fragment. Distinct from CJC-1295 with DAC.
peptides.mechanism: It is GRF(1-29) with amino-acid substitutions intended to slow enzymatic breakdown, so it still acts as a GHRH analog. Without the drug-affinity complex it does not bind albumin for a multi-day effect.
peptides.researchStatus: Not an FDA-approved medicine. It is often confused with the long-acting DAC form in casual writing.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary, frequently in the microgram range and more than once daily because the effect is brief. Those figures are not a labeled dose. Verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Commonly discussed vial sizes include 2 mg and 5 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Commonly cited near 30 minutes. That is why it is discussed as a short pulse rather than a weekly drug. Confirm independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Human safety data for this modified fragment are limited. Flushing and injection-site reactions are often described with GHRH analogs. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: CJC-1295 with DAC
peptides.summary: A GHRH analog attached to a drug-affinity complex that binds albumin and prolongs the effect.
peptides.mechanism: The peptide stimulates GHRH receptors. The affinity complex keeps it in circulation, so growth hormone and IGF-1 can stay elevated for days after a dose rather than for minutes.
peptides.researchStatus: Not an FDA-approved medicine. A 2006 pharmacokinetic study in people reported a half-life of about 6 to 8 days and sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation after single doses.
peptides.dosingNotes: That study used single subcutaneous doses scaled to body weight. It was a pharmacology study, not a regimen to copy. Commonly discussed schedules vary; verify independently. This is not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Research vials are often discussed at 2 mg or 5 mg. Dilution volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction. Do not assume it is interchangeable with the no-DAC fragment.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: About 6 to 8 days in the 2006 pharmacokinetic study. Weekly or less frequent discussion follows from that long half-life, unlike Mod GRF 1-29.
peptides.safetyNotes: Prolonged GH and IGF-1 elevation is a different risk profile from a brief pulse. The research record is small. In October 2026, a coroner in Victoria, Australia, found that a man died of anaphylaxis after self-injecting compounded CJC-1295 with ipamorelin, at double his prescribed amount, and recommended that the TGA review these peptides. Reports did not specify the DAC or no-DAC form. One case does not measure overall risk. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Sermorelin
peptides.summary: The 1-29 amino-acid fragment of growth hormone-releasing hormone, the shortest sequence that retains full GHRH activity in classic work.
peptides.mechanism: It binds pituitary GHRH receptors and stimulates growth-hormone release. It is not the same molecule as CJC-1295 or tesamorelin.
peptides.researchStatus: It was FDA-approved as Geref for evaluation and treatment of some growth-hormone deficiency settings and was later discontinued. It is not a currently marketed approved product in the US.
peptides.dosingNotes: Historical labeling used diagnostic and pediatric doses that are not a template for adult use. Commonly discussed adult ranges vary; verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: The discontinued product had its own diluent directions. Other vials are not that product. Volumes discussed for them are not standardized.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Very short, on the order of minutes, which is why more than one dose per day appears in older clinical use and in current discussion.
peptides.safetyNotes: Flushing, injection-site reactions, and antibody formation were described with the approved product. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Hexarelin
peptides.summary: A potent synthetic ghrelin-receptor agonist.
peptides.mechanism: It stimulates growth-hormone release and, unlike ipamorelin, is more often described as also affecting cortisol and prolactin. Repeated use is discussed as leading to a smaller growth-hormone response over time.
peptides.researchStatus: Not an FDA-approved medicine. Much of the human work is small endocrine studies rather than an approved regimen.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary and are usually in the microgram range. They are not a labeled dose. Verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often discussed at 2 mg or 5 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Short, commonly discussed as about an hour or less. Confirm independently. It is not a weekly compound.
peptides.safetyNotes: Water retention, hunger, cortisol and prolactin effects, and loss of effect with frequent dosing are the points most often raised. Human safety data are limited. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: GHRP-2
peptides.summary: A ghrelin-receptor agonist. In Japan, pralmorelin has been used as a growth-hormone stimulation test.
peptides.mechanism: It prompts pituitary growth-hormone release and can also raise cortisol, prolactin, and appetite more than ipamorelin in comparative descriptions.
peptides.researchStatus: A diagnostic use exists in some countries. It is not an FDA-approved therapeutic for body composition or performance.
peptides.dosingNotes: Diagnostic-test doses are not a daily regimen. Commonly discussed research ranges vary; verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Research vials are often listed at 5 mg or 10 mg. Dilution is not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Short-acting. Discussions usually describe one or more doses in a day, not weekly dosing. Confirm any half-life figure independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Hunger, cortisol, prolactin, and water retention are the effects most often cited. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: GHRP-6
peptides.summary: An earlier ghrelin mimetic, widely discussed and less selective than ipamorelin.
peptides.mechanism: It stimulates growth-hormone release via the ghrelin receptor and is particularly associated with hunger in descriptions of its effects.
peptides.researchStatus: Not an FDA-approved medicine.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary, usually in the microgram range and more than once daily. They are not a labeled dose. Verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often discussed at 5 mg or 10 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Short-acting. A precise half-life is not something to take from forum posts. Confirm independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Intense hunger, water retention, and cortisol or prolactin effects are commonly described. Human therapeutic safety is not established. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Ibutamoren
peptides.summary: An oral, non-peptide ghrelin-receptor agonist. Included because it is discussed beside injectable secretagogues.
peptides.mechanism: It activates the ghrelin receptor and raises growth hormone and IGF-1. It is taken by mouth, so there is no vial to reconstitute.
peptides.researchStatus: Not FDA-approved. Clinical studies have explored it for growth-hormone deficiency, older adults, and other settings. It has not become an approved drug.
peptides.dosingNotes: Published studies have used once-daily oral doses on the order of 10 mg to 25 mg. Those are trial doses, not a suggestion. Commonly discussed ranges outside the papers vary; verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Not a peptide vial. It is discussed as an oral liquid or capsule. Do not treat a research liquid concentration as a labeled product.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Long enough for once-daily oral dosing. A figure near 24 hours is commonly cited. Confirm in a primary source.
peptides.safetyNotes: Appetite increase, water retention, and effects on glucose and insulin are the findings most often reported from studies. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Retatrutide
peptides.summary: An investigational agonist at the GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors.
peptides.mechanism: The triple-agonist design is meant to combine incretin effects on glucose and appetite with glucagon-receptor activity. It is in development by Eli Lilly and is not an approved drug.
peptides.researchStatus: Investigational; not FDA-approved. A 2023 phase 2 trial appeared in the New England Journal of Medicine. In 2026, Eli Lilly reported phase 3 results, including TRIUMPH-1 in obesity and TRANSCEND-T2D-2, a head-to-head trial in type 2 diabetes in which it beat semaglutide (Ozempic) on blood sugar and weight loss. Lilly has said it plans to file with regulators in early 2027. In November 2026, two phase 3 trials in adults with knee osteoarthritis pain and obesity or overweight (TRIUMPH-4 and a knee-osteoarthritis analysis within TRIUMPH-1) were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and presented at ACR Convergence 2026; both reported greater reductions in knee pain and body weight than placebo. It remains unapproved.
peptides.dosingNotes: That phase 2 trial studied once-weekly doses from 1 mg up to 12 mg, with titration. Those are trial arms, not a personal regimen and not an approved dose. Verify in the paper. Commonly discussed ranges outside the trial vary.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: There is no approved vial or pen. Research-chemical presentations and any bacteriostatic-water ratios discussed for them are not standardized and are not the trial product. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Trials dose it once weekly. Treat specific half-life numbers from unofficial sources as unverified.
peptides.safetyNotes: Gastrointestinal effects are prominent in the incretin class. In the 2026 head-to-head phase 3 trial, diarrhea, dysesthesia (prickling or burning skin sensations), and discontinuations for side effects were more common than with semaglutide. Heart-rate changes and other trial safety findings belong to the published papers. It is unapproved. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Semaglutide
peptides.summary: A GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for type 2 diabetes and, in a separate product, chronic weight management.
peptides.mechanism: It slows gastric emptying, increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion, reduces glucagon, and reduces appetite. The oral tablet and the injections are different products.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved as Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus, each with its own indication and dose schedule.
peptides.dosingNotes: Labeled injectable schedules are once weekly and titrated. Ozempic labeling goes up to 2 mg weekly for diabetes. Wegovy labeling goes up to 2.4 mg weekly for weight management. Rybelsus is a daily tablet with its own doses. Read the current prescribing information. Unlabeled vial doses are not those products.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Approved injections are prefilled pens, not a lyophilized vial you mix with bacteriostatic water. Ratios discussed for research vials are not standardized and are not the labeled presentation.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: About one week, which is why the injections are weekly. The oral product is still taken daily because absorption, not half-life, limits it.
peptides.safetyNotes: Labeling includes gastrointestinal effects, gallbladder disease, pancreatitis risk language, and a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors from rodent data. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Tirzepatide
peptides.summary: A dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist.
peptides.mechanism: It activates both incretin receptors. Mounjaro is approved for type 2 diabetes and Zepbound for chronic weight management, among labeled uses that should be read from current prescribing information.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved as branded pens. Research vials are not those products.
peptides.dosingNotes: Labeled treatment starts at 2.5 mg once weekly and steps up. The highest labeled maintenance dose is 15 mg once weekly. That schedule is in the prescribing information and is not a suggestion to use an unapproved vial.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Approved product is a prefilled pen. Bacteriostatic-water ratios for lyophilized research vials are not standardized and are not the labeled pen.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: About five days. Labeling still uses once-weekly injections.
peptides.safetyNotes: Gastrointestinal effects are common. Labeling includes gallbladder, pancreatitis, and thyroid C-cell tumor warning language similar to other incretin drugs. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Liraglutide
peptides.summary: A daily GLP-1 receptor agonist, older than the weekly incretin drugs.
peptides.mechanism: Same incretin class as semaglutide: glucose-dependent insulin, lower glucagon, slower gastric emptying, and reduced appetite. Victoza and Saxenda are different labeled dose ranges for different indications.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved. Victoza is a diabetes product. Saxenda is a weight-management product.
peptides.dosingNotes: Both are once-daily injections with a titration in the prescribing information. Victoza labeling goes up to 1.8 mg daily. Saxenda labeling goes up to 3 mg daily. Those are labeled ceilings, not targets to copy from a research vial.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Approved product is a prefilled pen. It is not a bacteriostatic-water reconstitution.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: About 13 hours, which is why it is dosed every day rather than once a week.
peptides.safetyNotes: Gastrointestinal effects and the class warnings on the label, including thyroid C-cell tumor language, gallbladder disease, and pancreatitis. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Cagrilintide
peptides.summary: A long-acting amylin analog studied alone and together with semaglutide. The combination is often called CagriSema.
peptides.mechanism: Amylin agonism slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite through a different receptor from GLP-1. Combination trials pair it with semaglutide.
peptides.researchStatus: Investigational. Not FDA-approved as a single agent or as the combination. Novo Nordisk filed a New Drug Application for CagriSema for weight management in December 2025, and an FDA decision is expected in late 2026. Filing is not approval.
peptides.dosingNotes: Published trials have used once-weekly subcutaneous doses in the low milligram range, with titration. Read the trial papers for the exact arms. Commonly discussed ranges outside those papers vary; verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: No approved presentation. Research-vial dilutions are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Designed for once-weekly dosing. Use the papers rather than a forum half-life.
peptides.safetyNotes: Gastrointestinal effects are expected from this class. Long-term safety is still a trial question. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Survodutide
peptides.summary: An investigational dual agonist at the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors.
peptides.mechanism: GLP-1 activity addresses appetite and glucose. Glucagon-receptor activity is being studied for energy expenditure and liver fat. It is not retatrutide and it is not tirzepatide.
peptides.researchStatus: Investigational, developed by Boehringer Ingelheim. Not FDA-approved. Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE results presented in 2026, including SYNCHRONIZE-2 in people with type 2 diabetes, showed weight loss over placebo. A separate cardiovascular outcomes trial is ongoing.
peptides.dosingNotes: Phase 2 work used once-weekly subcutaneous injections with titration. Exact arms belong in the papers. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: No approved vial. Research dilutions are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Trial designs use once-weekly dosing. A precise half-life should come from the sponsor's publications.
peptides.safetyNotes: Gastrointestinal effects and heart-rate findings have been reported in trial coverage. Unapproved. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: MOTS-c
aliases: Mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA type-c
peptides.summary: A mitochondrial-derived peptide studied in metabolic and exercise models.
peptides.mechanism: It is encoded in mitochondrial DNA and has been studied for effects on skeletal muscle and insulin sensitivity, largely in cells and animals.
peptides.researchStatus: Preclinical and early research. Not an approved drug. Human dosing is not established. In October 2026, HHS issued a draft, interim enforcement-discretion policy (Federal Register, Oct 30, 2026; comments through Nov 13) under which it does not intend to act against state-licensed 503A pharmacies compounding this peptide when specific conditions are met, such as identity, route, sourcing, testing, and adverse-event reporting. That is not FDA approval, not a 503A bulks-list addition, and it can be revisited.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. There is no labeled dose.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vial sizes in listings vary, often 10 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Not well defined for human dosing. Do not import an animal-study interval as a schedule.
peptides.safetyNotes: Human safety is largely unknown. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: BPC-157
peptides.summary: A synthetic pentadecapeptide related to a sequence in gastric juice protein. Most evidence is preclinical.
peptides.mechanism: Animal and cell studies have explored wound, tendon, gut, and blood-vessel models. A single human mechanism is not established. Stable gastric forms and injectable forms are both discussed and are not the same evidence base.
peptides.researchStatus: Not FDA-approved. Human trials are sparse relative to the volume of animal papers and online discussion. In October 2026, HHS issued a draft, interim enforcement-discretion policy (Federal Register, Oct 30, 2026; comments through Nov 13) under which it does not intend to act against state-licensed 503A pharmacies compounding this peptide when specific conditions are met, such as identity, route, sourcing, testing, and adverse-event reporting. That is not FDA approval, not a 503A bulks-list addition, and it can be revisited.
peptides.dosingNotes: A human dose is not established. Commonly discussed ranges vary widely, including both injection and oral amounts. Verify independently. This is not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Listings often mention 5 mg or 10 mg vials. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. Oral products are a different presentation. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Thought to be short. Once- or twice-daily discussion is common and is not the same as a measured human half-life. Confirm independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Limited human safety data. Theoretical concerns include unwanted blood-vessel growth. Quality of research-chemical supply is unverified. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: TB-500
peptides.summary: A name used for a synthetic fragment of thymosin beta-4. It is easy to confuse with the full protein.
peptides.mechanism: Thymosin beta-4 research, mostly preclinical, has looked at actin binding, cell migration, and wound models. The fragment sold as TB-500 is not automatically the same material or dose as full-length thymosin beta-4.
peptides.researchStatus: Not FDA-approved. Human evidence for the fragment is limited. In October 2026, HHS issued a draft, interim enforcement-discretion policy (Federal Register, Oct 30, 2026; comments through Nov 13) under which it does not intend to act against state-licensed 503A pharmacies compounding this peptide when specific conditions are met, such as identity, route, sourcing, testing, and adverse-event reporting. That is not FDA approval, not a 503A bulks-list addition, and it can be revisited.
peptides.dosingNotes: A human dose is not established. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. Do not copy a veterinary or animal dose.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often listed at 2 mg, 5 mg, or 10 mg. Dilution volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Not well established for the fragment in people. Weekly discussion is a forum pattern, not a measured schedule you should assume is correct.
peptides.safetyNotes: Human safety is not established. Confusing it with full thymosin beta-4, or with thymosin alpha-1, is a common labeling problem. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: GHK-Cu
peptides.summary: A copper complex of a tripeptide that occurs naturally in human plasma, studied mostly for skin.
peptides.mechanism: Laboratory and cosmetic research has looked at collagen, wound models, and antioxidant effects of the copper complex. Topical cosmetic use and injection are different claims.
peptides.researchStatus: Used in cosmetics. Not an FDA-approved injectable drug.
peptides.dosingNotes: Cosmetic concentrations are product-specific and topical. Injectable amounts discussed online vary and are not an approved dose. Verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Injectable listings often cite 50 mg or 100 mg vials. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. Topical serums are not reconstituted the same way. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: A practical injection interval is not established from cosmetic research. Confirm any cited half-life independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Copper load, injection-site irritation, and the gap between topical cosmetics and injection are the relevant caveats. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: KPV
peptides.summary: The C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone, studied in inflammation models.
peptides.mechanism: Preclinical work has explored anti-inflammatory effects in gut and skin models. It does not share the pigmentary reputation of full melanocortin agonists such as melanotan II.
peptides.researchStatus: Preclinical. Not an approved drug. Human dosing is not established. In October 2026, HHS issued a draft, interim enforcement-discretion policy (Federal Register, Oct 30, 2026; comments through Nov 13) under which it does not intend to act against state-licensed 503A pharmacies compounding this peptide when specific conditions are met, such as identity, route, sourcing, testing, and adverse-event reporting. That is not FDA approval, not a 503A bulks-list addition, and it can be revisited.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary, including oral and injectable mentions. Verify independently. There is no labeled dose.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vial sizes in listings vary. Dilution is not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Not established for a human schedule. Short peptides are often discussed as daily. That is not a measured half-life.
peptides.safetyNotes: Human safety data are minimal. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Selank
peptides.summary: A synthetic tuftsin analog developed in Russian research and discussed for anxiety.
peptides.mechanism: It is based on the immune peptide tuftsin with an added Pro-Gly-Pro tail, and it has been studied as an intranasal anxiolytic in Russian-language clinical literature. It is not a benzodiazepine.
peptides.researchStatus: It has been registered as a medicine in Russia. It is not FDA-approved.
peptides.dosingNotes: Russian product information describes intranasal use. Copying a dose from a secondary summary is a bad idea; read the source. Commonly discussed ranges elsewhere vary; verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: The researched route is intranasal drops, not a typical insulin-syringe reconstitution. Injectable discussion is a separate, less documented practice.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Intranasal courses in the product literature are short daily courses rather than a weekly injection. Confirm the schedule in the source document.
peptides.safetyNotes: Evidence outside the Russian development program is limited. Not medical advice, and not a substitute for care of an anxiety disorder.

peptides.name: Semax
peptides.summary: A synthetic analog of an ACTH fragment, developed in Russia and discussed for attention and neurologic recovery.
peptides.mechanism: It is derived from ACTH(4-10) with a Pro-Gly-Pro tail and has been studied intranasally. It is not melatonin, and it is not selank.
peptides.researchStatus: Used as a medicine in Russia for certain neurologic indications. Not FDA-approved. In October 2026, HHS issued a draft, interim enforcement-discretion policy (Federal Register, Oct 30, 2026; comments through Nov 13) under which it does not intend to act against state-licensed 503A pharmacies compounding this peptide when specific conditions are met, such as identity, route, sourcing, testing, and adverse-event reporting. That is not FDA approval, not a 503A bulks-list addition, and it can be revisited.
peptides.dosingNotes: Product strengths and drop regimens belong to that labeling. Commonly discussed ranges outside it vary; verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: The established presentation is nasal drops at a labeled concentration, not a bacteriostatic-water vial. Research vials are a different product.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Labeling describes divided daytime intranasal doses during a course, which fits a short-acting peptide. Confirm any half-life number independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Do not treat a research-chemical vial as the registered nasal drug. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Epitalon
peptides.summary: A synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) studied by the Khavinson group in relation to epithalamin, a pineal extract.
peptides.mechanism: Those papers discuss pineal function and, in some experiments, telomerase. Independent replication is limited. It is not melatonin.
peptides.researchStatus: Not approved as a drug in the US or the EU. Much of the human literature comes from one research network. In October 2026, HHS issued a draft, interim enforcement-discretion policy (Federal Register, Oct 30, 2026; comments through Nov 13) under which it does not intend to act against state-licensed 503A pharmacies compounding this peptide when specific conditions are met, such as identity, route, sourcing, testing, and adverse-event reporting. That is not FDA approval, not a 503A bulks-list addition, and it can be revisited.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed course lengths vary, often as a short cycle rather than continuous use. A standardized human dose is not established. Verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often listed at 10 mg or 50 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Not well characterized. Discussion usually describes a daily injection for a limited number of days. That pattern is not a measured half-life.
peptides.safetyNotes: Limited independent human safety data. Anti-aging claims run ahead of the evidence. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Bremelanotide
peptides.summary: A melanocortin receptor agonist approved for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women.
peptides.mechanism: It acts on melanocortin receptors in the nervous system rather than on blood vessels the way PDE5 inhibitors do. The approved population and setting are narrow.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved as Vyleesi for acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women. Use in men, or for other reasons, is outside that approval.
peptides.dosingNotes: The labeled dose is 1.75 mg subcutaneously as needed, at least 45 minutes before sexual activity, at most one dose in 24 hours, and not more than eight doses in a month. That is labeling, not a suggestion to exceed it or to use a research vial.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: The approved product is a single-use autoinjector. Research vials are not that device, and mixing ratios for them are not the label.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: About 2.7 hours in the prescribing information.
peptides.safetyNotes: Nausea, flushing, headache, blood-pressure increases, and hyperpigmentation are on the label, including darkened skin and gums that may not fully resolve. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Melanotan II
peptides.summary: An unapproved cyclic analog of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone, discussed for tanning and sexual effects.
peptides.mechanism: It is a nonselective melanocortin agonist, so pigment cells, appetite, and sexual arousal can all be affected. It is not the same molecule as afamelanotide or bremelanotide.
peptides.researchStatus: Not FDA-approved. It has been sold through unregulated channels. Early academic work exists; it is not a licensed tanning drug.
peptides.dosingNotes: There is no approved dose. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. Loading and maintenance schedules online are not a protocol from a regulator.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often listed at 10 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Commonly described as lasting hours, with pigment changes that persist longer than the drug. Confirm any number independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Nausea, flushing, spontaneous erections, blood-pressure changes, new or darkening moles, and unknown purity of unregulated products are the serious caveats. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Afamelanotide
peptides.summary: A linear alpha-MSH analog. The approved product is a clinician-administered implant for erythropoietic protoporphyria.
peptides.mechanism: It increases melanin and is used, under supervision, to reduce photosensitivity in erythropoietic protoporphyria. It is not melanotan II and it is not a home injectable.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved as Scenesse for erythropoietic protoporphyria. The implant is placed by a trained professional.
peptides.dosingNotes: The labeled product is a 16 mg implant about every two months, given in a clinic. That is not a vial dose and not a tanning regimen.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: There is no patient reconstitution. Research vials sold as melanotan I are not the Scenesse implant.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: The implant is designed to release the drug over time. The dosing interval is about 60 days in labeling.
peptides.safetyNotes: Pigment changes, nausea, and mole surveillance are part of the clinical picture. Using an unregulated vial to imitate the implant is not the approved treatment. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Kisspeptin-10
peptides.summary: A short fragment of kisspeptin, a hormone that stimulates GnRH release.
peptides.mechanism: Kisspeptin neurons drive the reproductive axis. The 10-amino-acid fragment has been used in clinical research on hormone pulses, puberty, and reproductive function.
peptides.researchStatus: An investigational and research tool. Not an FDA-approved therapeutic.
peptides.dosingNotes: Published infusions and injections use study-specific amounts, often intravenous. Those protocols are not a home dose. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Research vials are a different setting from a controlled infusion study. Dilution is not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Short. Study schedules are often infusions or brief injections, not a weekly depot.
peptides.safetyNotes: Effects on the reproductive axis mean it is not a casual add-on. Human use outside a study is not an approved treatment. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Gonadorelin
peptides.summary: Synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone, historically used as a diagnostic test of the pituitary-gonadal axis.
peptides.mechanism: A pulse of GnRH stimulates the pituitary to release LH and FSH. Continuous exposure can suppress that axis instead, which is the principle behind longer-acting GnRH analogs used in medicine. Those are different drugs.
peptides.researchStatus: Diagnostic products have been approved and some have been discontinued. It is not a do-it-yourself fertility or post-cycle protocol.
peptides.dosingNotes: Diagnostic doses in older labeling are single tests, not a recurring stack. Commonly discussed repeated schedules vary and are not the diagnostic test. Verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Any leftover diagnostic kit had its own directions. Research vials do not inherit that label. Volumes are not standardized.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Minutes. The physiologic signal is pulsatile. A single long-acting exposure is a different endocrine maneuver.
peptides.safetyNotes: It moves LH, FSH, and sex steroids. Using it without laboratory follow-up is not a benign experiment. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Oxytocin
peptides.summary: A peptide hormone used in obstetrics, and separately studied intranasally in behavioral research.
peptides.mechanism: Hospital oxytocin stimulates uterine contraction and is part of labor and delivery care. Intranasal research has looked at social behavior. Those are different uses and different products.
peptides.researchStatus: FDA-approved as an intravenous or intramuscular obstetric drug given in a monitored setting. Behavioral nasal research is not that approval.
peptides.dosingNotes: Obstetric doses are titrated in a hospital and are dangerous outside that setting. Intranasal research amounts vary by study. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Pitocin is a sterile solution for hospital use, not a bacteriostatic-water research vial. Do not reconstitute or dose it from this catalog.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: A few minutes in the blood, which is why obstetric infusions are continuous. Nasal research has its own timing.
peptides.safetyNotes: Hospital oxytocin can cause uterine rupture, fetal distress, and water intoxication if misused. It is not a research-chemical project. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: AOD-9604
peptides.summary: A modified fragment of human growth hormone covering residues 176-191, studied for fat metabolism.
peptides.mechanism: The fragment was designed to keep a lipolytic region of growth hormone without the growth-promoting effects of the full hormone. Trial results did not turn it into an approved obesity drug. It is not identical to unmodified fragment 176-191.
peptides.researchStatus: Not FDA-approved. Obesity and cartilage studies exist. It has also drawn regulatory warnings when sold as a supplement.
peptides.dosingNotes: Trial doses should be read from the papers. Commonly discussed daily microgram or milligram ranges vary; verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Research vials are often listed at 2 mg or 5 mg. Oral and injectable forms are both discussed and are not interchangeable. Dilution is not standardized.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Often discussed as a daily compound. A precise half-life should come from a paper, not a product page.
peptides.safetyNotes: It is not an approved weight-loss medicine. Confusing it with full growth hormone, or with unmodified fragment 176-191, matters. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: hGH fragment 176-191
peptides.summary: The unmodified C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone, residues 176 through 191.
peptides.mechanism: This region has been studied for fat-cell lipolysis without the full hormone's IGF-1 effect. AOD-9604 is a modified cousin, not the same sequence.
peptides.researchStatus: Not an approved drug. Evidence is mostly preclinical plus a thin human record.
peptides.dosingNotes: A human dose is not established. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often listed at 2 mg, 5 mg, or 10 mg. Bacteriostatic-water volumes are not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Short enough that discussion is usually once or twice daily. Confirm any cited half-life independently.
peptides.safetyNotes: Do not assume the safety data for AOD-9604, or for full growth hormone, apply to this fragment. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: LL-37
peptides.summary: The active human cathelicidin peptide, part of innate antibacterial defense.
peptides.mechanism: It disrupts microbial membranes and also signals immune cells. It is not a simple antibiotic, and it can be proinflammatory. Research includes infection, wound, and cancer models.
peptides.researchStatus: An endogenous peptide and a research compound. Not an FDA-approved drug.
peptides.dosingNotes: No established therapeutic dose for self-administration. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Research vials are uncommon and concentrations vary. Dilution is not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: It is degraded by the body and is not a weekly depot. A dosing interval is not established.
peptides.safetyNotes: Proinflammatory activity and the lack of an approved product are the main caveats. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Thymosin alpha-1
peptides.summary: A thymic peptide used in several countries as an immune modulator, including for chronic hepatitis B.
peptides.mechanism: It is thought to support T-cell and dendritic-cell function. It is not thymosin beta-4 and not TB-500.
peptides.researchStatus: Marketed as Zadaxin in a number of countries. It is not an FDA-approved drug in the United States.
peptides.dosingNotes: Zadaxin labeling outside the United States describes 1.6 mg subcutaneously, often twice a week in hepatitis B regimens. That is foreign product labeling, not a US approval and not a suggestion to import or compound it.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Zadaxin is supplied as a 1.6 mg lyophilized vial with its own diluent directions. Other vials are not that product. Follow a real package insert only for that product, and do not invent a ratio here.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: The foreign label uses an intermittent subcutaneous schedule rather than a daily one. Confirm the interval in the current package insert.
peptides.safetyNotes: It is a real medicine in some jurisdictions and an unapproved drug in the US. Immune effects are not automatically benign. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: DSIP
peptides.summary: A peptide isolated in sleep research in the 1970s. Later human results have been inconsistent.
peptides.mechanism: It was named for an effect on delta sleep in early animal experiments. It has not become a reliable hypnotic, and the mechanism in people is unsettled. It is not melatonin and not a benzodiazepine.
peptides.researchStatus: Experimental. Not an approved sleep medicine. Small older human studies disagree with each other.
peptides.dosingNotes: Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. There is no established clinical dose. Not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Vials are often listed at 2 mg, 5 mg, or 15 mg. Dilution is not standardized. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Short. Evening dosing is the usual discussion because of the sleep claim, not because a modern pharmacokinetic profile exists.
peptides.safetyNotes: Do not assume it causes sleep. Evidence is weak and mixed. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: IGF-1 LR3
peptides.summary: A modified insulin-like growth factor-1 analog with longer activity than native IGF-1.
peptides.mechanism: Amino-acid changes reduce binding to IGF binding proteins, so more of the peptide stays available to the IGF-1 receptor. That also means hypoglycemia is a direct risk, as with insulin-family signaling.
peptides.researchStatus: A laboratory reagent and an unapproved drug. It is not recombinant human IGF-1 (mecasermin), which is a separate approved medicine for defined growth disorders.
peptides.dosingNotes: There is no established dose for self-administration. Commonly discussed ranges vary; verify independently. Mecasermin dosing on its own label does not transfer to LR3.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: Research vials are often listed at 0.1 mg or 1 mg, sometimes in acetic acid rather than bacteriostatic water because the peptide can be unstable. Handling notes on a chemical supplier page are not a clinical recipe.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Longer than native IGF-1. A once-daily discussion is common and is still not an approved schedule.
peptides.safetyNotes: Hypoglycemia, edema, and the growth-promoting signal of IGF-1 are serious. This is one of the higher-risk entries in the catalog. Not medical advice.

peptides.name: Efpeglenatide
peptides.summary: A long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist from Hanmi Pharmaceutical, approved in South Korea in 2026 as Eppe for chronic weight management.
peptides.mechanism: It is an exendin-4-based GLP-1 receptor agonist joined to an antibody fragment through Hanmi's LAPSCOVERY platform, which extends its duration of action. Like other GLP-1 agonists, it reduces appetite and slows gastric emptying. It is not semaglutide.
peptides.researchStatus: Approved by South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety in October 2026 as Eppe for weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, who do not have diabetes. Prescriptions began on October 29, 2026. A Korean phase 3 trial reported about 10% average weight loss at 40 weeks. Not FDA-approved.
peptides.dosingNotes: Approved strengths and the titration schedule belong to the Korean labeling. Follow the prescriber and that label. This is not a dose for you and not a recommendation.
peptides.reconstitutionNotes: The approved product is a prefilled autoinjector, not a vial for reconstitution. Research-vial versions, if any, are not the approved product. This is not a reconstitution instruction.
peptides.halfLifeNotes: Designed for once-weekly injection. A precise half-life should come from the labeling or the sponsor's publications.
peptides.safetyNotes: Gastrointestinal effects are expected from the GLP-1 class. Class warnings and contraindications are in the labeling. Not medical advice.
